data.narrative:
Hgen is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Colin Ho and Molly Yang that has raised $7M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers spanning battery materials, hydrogen, and critical minerals. However, narrow peer comparables—those at the same stage or adjacent stage with similar valuation tier—are insufficient in count (fewer than 3) to support a reliable peer-median multiple analysis.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation lens. Using total capital raised ($7M) as a proxy for current implied value and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied post-seed valuation of $18M. This approach assumes Hgen's capital efficiency and burn profile align with median frontier-tech seed progression.

The triangulated valuation range is $15M to $20M, with a median point of $18M, derived from a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the timing and terms of the next funding event, Hgen's actual revenue or unit progress relative to stage expectations, and whether public comp multiples (LNZA) or later-stage private valuations (Redwood, QuantumScape) prove instructive once additional climate-tech seed companies reach later funding rounds. This single-method result should be stress-tested against management projections and forthcoming interim milestones.
